methods.name: hello
methods.description: The handshake; must come first on every connection. Another product or protocol is refused with `SHED_VERSION`.

schema.description: The product, `shed`; a peer that sends none is refused like another protocol.
The git commit the sender was built from.
The sender's [`PROTOCOL`]; a peer that sends none counts as protocol 0.

methods.name: run
methods.description: Start a terminal. `name` defaults to the first free `tN`; `keep` brings it back as a shell in its cwd after a server restart; `rows` and `cols` default to `$SHED_SIZE` (`RxC`) of the server, else 50x200. ACP: `mcp_servers` (stdio, `http`, `sse`, in ACP's shapes) go to the agent; their env and header values are never saved or shown. `meta` (an object) goes unchanged as the session's `_meta`. `no_hibernate` keeps the agent running when idle. `parent` links it to the terminal that started it: when the parent's program ends the child is killed too, unless `outlive`; with `notify` a `[shed] <name> blocked|error|exited …` line is typed into the parent (a prompt for an ACP parent) when the child blocks, errors or ends, once per piece of news, held while the parent reports `working`.

schema.description: The terminal's name, unique per server; `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`.
Come back as a shell after a server restart.
Report `idle` after this many seconds without output, until the program reports a state.

The program and its arguments; with `acp`, the agent's ACP adapter (empty: the installed
agent's), which the server wraps in its own bridge.
The ACP agent the program bridges (`shed run --acp`): `read` renders its transcript.
ACP: how the bridge answers permission requests (default `ask`).
ACP: load this agent session (`session/load`, `$SHED_ACP_RESUME` to the bridge) instead of a new one.

ACP: MCP servers for the agent, in ACP's shapes: stdio `{name, command, args, env}`, or
`{type: "http" | "sse", name, url, headers}`. Kept in memory only; send them again to resume.

ACP: the session's options, sent unchanged as `_meta` on `session/new` and `session/load`;
which keys exist is the agent's business. Callers: drover (herdsman#923) and cooee.
ACP: never hibernate the agent when idle.
Start it on this machine, over its held link (`machine.links`).
The terminal that started it (`shed run` sends `$SHED`).

methods.name: ls
methods.description: List terminals, by name; `labels` keeps those that carry every given label, `parent` the children of that terminal.

schema.description: Only terminals carrying every one of these labels.
Only the children of this terminal.

methods.name: get
methods.description: One terminal.

methods.name: read
methods.description: The visible screen, or with `history` the scrollback and screen, as plain text; `lines` keeps the last N lines. ACP: the transcript as text, or with `events` its events (each with its `seq`), paged by `before` and `n`.

schema.description: Scrollback and screen instead of the screen alone.
ACP: the transcript's events instead of text.

methods.name: send
methods.description: Type text into the terminal.

methods.name: keys
methods.description: Press keys by name (`enter`, `esc`, `ctrl+c`, `up`, …); nothing is sent if any name is unknown.

methods.name: kill
methods.description: End the terminal's whole process tree (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL); returns the exited terminal.

methods.name: rm
methods.description: Remove an exited terminal; returns it as it was.

methods.name: resize
methods.description: Resize the terminal; the program gets SIGWINCH.

methods.name: attach
methods.description: Take over the terminal. After the response the server writes a redraw (clear, then the screen text) and the program's raw output, and closes the connection when the program's PTY closes. The client sends only notifications from then on (`send`, `keys`, `resize`); detaching is closing the connection.

methods.name: state
methods.description: Report the terminal's state (`working`, `blocked`, `done` or `error`) with an optional note; a program can also print `ESC ] 7501 ; state=<s>[;note=<n>] BEL`, which never reaches the screen.

schema.description: The other agent's escape the state came from, e.g. `jan-osc9999`; absent for shed's own.

methods.name: wait
methods.description: Answer once the reported state is one of `until` (`idle` too, from the `idle_after` fallback) or a visible screen line matches the pattern `output` (`matched`), the program exits (`exited`) or `timeout` seconds pass (`timeout`). The server blocks; nothing polls. With `children`, `name` is a parent: `all` matches once no child is working (`terminal` is the parent), `any` on the next child that reports `done`, `blocked` or `error`, or exits (`terminal` is that child; `exited` when no child runs).

schema.description: The terminal's name; with `children`, the parent's.
Wait on the terminal's children instead of the terminal.
Reported states that end the wait.
A pattern (`.`, `[…]`, `\d \w \s`, `* + ?`, `^ $`) that ends the wait when a screen line matches.
Give up after this many seconds; none waits for ever.

methods.name: events
methods.description: Stream events. After the response the server writes one event per line (see Events) for the terminals carrying every one of `labels`, first those after `since` still in the ring of the last 1,000, and never closes the connection; closing it unsubscribes.

schema.description: Only events of terminals carrying every one of these labels.
Replay the kept events whose `seq` is above this one first.

methods.name: emit
methods.description: Emit one of an ACP terminal's structured events (`turn`, `text`, `tool_call`, `plan`, `mode`, `approval_request`, `approved`, `reply`); its bridge (`shed run --acp`) calls this. Other events are refused.

The reported state changed.

methods.name: screen.watch
methods.description: Stream a running terminal's screen. After the response the server writes screen updates (see Screen updates), at most 20 a second: the full screen first (none when `since` is the screen's current `seq`), then the rows that changed. It closes the connection when the program's PTY closes. The connection still takes requests; their responses are not written.

schema.description: The `seq` of the last update the client applied: no full screen first if nothing changed since.

methods.name: terminal.input
methods.description: Type text into the terminal, as `send`.

methods.name: terminal.keys
methods.description: Press keys by name, as `keys`; `ctrl-x` is `ctrl+x`.

methods.name: terminal.resize
methods.description: Resize the terminal, as `resize`; without `terminal`, the one this connection watches.

schema.description: The terminal's name; default the one this connection watches.

methods.name: terminal.readonly
methods.description: Mark the terminal read-only for this connection: from then on, until it closes, the connection's `send`, `keys`, `resize`, `attach`, `terminal.input`, `terminal.keys` and `terminal.resize` to the terminal are refused with `READONLY`. The connection may resize only the terminals it has not marked.

methods.name: machine.stats
methods.description: The machine's health now: load per CPU, memory pressure (percent of memory not available), swap used, free space on the volume of the state file, CPUs, uptime and the terminals by state (the reported state while running, else `running`; `exited`). The server keeps one sample a minute for 24 h; `since` (unix seconds) adds those after it as `history`.

schema.description: Add the kept samples taken after this time (unix seconds) as `history`.

methods.name: acp.model
methods.description: Switch an ACP terminal's model to one of its `session.models`: its bridge asks the agent (`session/set_config_option`, the `model` option) and emits `session` with the new `model`.

schema.description: The model id, one of the session's `models`.

methods.name: machine.links
methods.description: Each configured machine's held link: `up`, `reconnecting` or `down`, since when, and why it is down. A request naming `<machine>/<name>` (`get`, `read`, `send`, `keys`, `kill`, `rm`, `state`, `acp.model`, `wait`; `run` with `machine`, ACP ones bridged by that server) goes over the link; `ls` and `events` include every machine, their names so prefixed. Reads the config again, linking machines added since.

methods.name: exec
methods.description: Run a program without a terminal in a process group of its own, `stdin` fed to it, and answer with its exit code (128 + the signal when one ended it) and the exact bytes it wrote. The group is ended when the program returns or `timeout` seconds pass (`IO`); output over `REPLY_LIMIT` bytes is `IO`, never cut. `machine` runs it there, over the held link.

schema.description: Its working directory; default the server's.
End it after this many seconds.
Bytes fed to its stdin, then closed.
Run it on this machine, over its held link.

methods.name: file.read
methods.description: A file's bytes; one over `REPLY_LIMIT` bytes is `IO`. `machine` reads it there.

schema.description: The machine it is on, over its held link.

methods.name: file.write
methods.description: Replace a file with `data`: written to a temp file beside it, then renamed over it, its mode kept. `machine` writes it there.

schema.description: The machine it is on, over its held link.

methods.name: rpc.discover
methods.description: The whole API as one OpenRPC document, as `shed schema` prints it (`docs/shed.openrpc.json`): every method's params and result, the streamed events and screen updates, and the error codes, as JSON Schema. Needs no `hello`.
